svg.title: sky jobs launch workflow on ej-prj-i2-6
svg.text: sky jobs launch: workflow, functions, line numbers and measured times
Code: ej-prj-i2-6 407784c57 (on master 796c5bcc8). Consolidation mode (sky api start --deploy). Task: ej/task_bytecode.yaml, 6 nodes on k8s/kind-skypilot, one echo.
Times are medians in seconds. The letter beside a time says where it comes from. O1–O14 mark the rows each optimization changed; the list is at the bottom.
latest A/B: ej-prj-i2-5 vs ej-prj-i2-6, 8 runs per arm (20261102-i2-6-ab)
phase A profile: 24 hooked runs, client-side times (20261102-phase-a-profile)
older trace, before later commits; relative size only (see the notes)

HTTP or signal across processes · :N = line
separate process, on the API server host
Largest wait in A. With no storage cloud enabled, the
check re-runs on every launch. 3.49 s for all of A without
Render and run the controller script
Mostly one wait: a new Python process runs the scheduler.
Ask the API server for a cluster
Nearly all of C is one AWS credential check. C is 0.98 s
without aws on the server PATH.
Starts 0.83 s into D. Range in the A/B: 1.5–2.3 s.
These runs set IfNotPresent. The template still sets
Always, which added 6 serial pull checks on one kind node:
Range in the A/B: 1.5–11.6 s. These stalls are not fixed.
A uv lock held by the PyPI dry run is the likely cause.
Runs on its own from container start, not traced here. T
times: A/B of O10 + O11, before the final image.
ray stop only if Ray runs
Wait for Ray; start skylet alongside
Largest stage left in D, down from 16.28 s on the base
before all changes. Skylet finishes first, so the wait for
workers to join sets the time.
Without gRPC, each starts Python on the head over kubectl
exec. gRPC is off by default. _add_job runs on into E.
From queue → last rank. Not visible from the server. T
rows are an older trace on the published image, 8.32 s in
all, so bytecode has likely cut the import rows.
Overlaps E, so it does not set E's length. It does decide
when the status check runs, and so sets F. Caller of the
Check status, mark the job RUNNING
Both are head commands. The first began before the job
ended; 0.97 s of it falls in F.
No recorded wait: no head command when the launch already
saw SUCCEEDED. Otherwise: wait up to 15 s, then one
command for status and end time.
Follower waits for saved logs, then exits
SUCCEEDED usually arrives before the follower tails the
cluster (10 of 11 runs), so a short job's logs appear in
one burst at the end. The rest of H is the client's own
Save logs and tear down the cluster
Starts after SUCCEEDED. The client waits for the log copy
but not for the probe or teardown, which runs on after it

Phase numbers beside each band: ej-prj-i2-5 → ej-prj-i2-6, same session, 8 runs per arm, with the permutation p. Client total 41.3 → 40.0 s (p = 0.19). Breakdown rows come from a separate traced session, whose

phase medians are listed in the table above, so they can differ slightly. The hook made no significant difference to phase times in the earlier trace (34.81 vs 35.13 s, p = 0.97); it was not re-tested for the
extra timers, and 1 of 15 traced launches failed at submission.

Phases A and C depend on the API server's PATH. With .venv/bin on it, as here, the storage check also runs the aws CLI. A controlled test, same code: A 3.49 vs 7.03 s, and C 0.98 vs 3.42 s, 4 measured runs per
arm (20261102-aws-path-test). The time without aws is shown in those boxes.
Against master: 796c5bcc8 + published image → ej-prj-i2-5 + bytecode image, 79.1 → 45.0 s for sky jobs launch, and 44.13 → 29.67 s for sky launch. ej-prj-i2-6 has no direct A/B against master.

Overlap: rows do not always add up to their box. Pods bootstrap while the provisioner runs, skylet starts during the Ray wait, and the controller's checks overlap E and H. T times predate later commits and show

Conditions: 6 nodes on kind, one machine, IfNotPresent with the local bytecode image, gRPC off, consolidation mode. The first launch after a server restart is slower (warm-ups were dropped). The bytecode image
Not shown: failure and recovery paths, and _submit_remotely() without consolidation mode.
